claims: Average token spend per question: extra high = 338 tokens, max = 4,970 tokens (~15x)
That 15x token increase bought only ~1% better output on the benchmark
Conclusion: 'do not even bother with the max setting' when building with Claude
Max effort is labelled in the Claude UI as '5.5x or more usage'
how_to_steps: Open the Effort picker in Claude (Low / Medium / High / Extra / Max)
Leave it on Extra (xhigh) for building; do not select Max
Compare xhigh vs max rows in the benchmark table to see accuracy is nearly identical while tokens/cost explode
on_screen_only: Title card: 'CLAUDE EFFORT LEVEL MATTERS MORE THEN YOU THINK' / 'TOKEN HACKING EPISODE 10'

Benchmark table (Model | Tests | % Right | Errors): kimi-k3 60%, muse-spark-1.3 82%, grok-4.5 76%, gemini-3.1-pro-preview 95%, claude-sonnet-5-xhigh 37%, claude-sonnet-5-max 57%, claude-opus-5-xhigh 83%, claude-opus-5-max 83%, claude-fable-5-xhigh 84%, claude-fable-5-max 82%, claude-opus-5.5-xhigh 78% (circled), claude-opus-5.5-max 79% (circled), claude-opus-4.8-xhigh 74%, claude-opus-4.8-max 75%, claude-4.6-sonnet 66%, claude-4.5-opus-thinking-high 62%, claude-4.6-opus-thinking-high 70%, gpt-5.4-xhigh 80%, gpt-5-high 78% -- all 390/390 tests
A wider version of the same table shows per-model $ cost and token columns (e.g. values ~$0.04-$0.19 and token counts 118 to 4,970) with one cell circled in red
NOTE: the on-screen table contradicts the blanket advice for Sonnet 5: xhigh 37% vs max 57% (a 20-point jump); fable-5 max (82%) actually scored lower than xhigh (84%)
cta: none beyond 'keep building, see you tomorrow' (daily series)

relevance.why: Haji runs Claude Code on a subscription with weekly limits; effort level is a one-click lever that directly controls burn. The number (15x tokens for 1%) is the kind of concrete, zero-effort rule he can apply today.

implement_score.why: Zero cost: set /effort to extra-high (not max) as the default for Claude Code and Cowork sessions; reserve max for a single hard reasoning task. Caveat from the table itself: for Sonnet-class models max helped a lot, so the rule is 'skip max on Opus/Fable', not universally.
